articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft patched a jaw-dropping 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and the deliciously named 'BlueHammer' Windows Defender flaw. When your Patch Tuesday looks like a phone book, maybe it's time to rethink that security-by-obscurity strategy.

articles.title: Meta U-turns on encryption push for Instagram as DMs go plaintext
articles.summary: 'Dirty Frag' delivers root access to all major Linux distros with zero patches available and a public exploit in the wild. Someone broke disclosure protocol and left admins holding the bag—this is why we can't have nice things.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: ShinyHunters ransacked Canvas during finals week, disrupting education for millions of students nationwide. Nothing says 'digital learning revolution' like having your homework held hostage by cybercriminals.

articles.title: Canvas Got Hacked During Finals Week and Students Are Freaking Out
articles.summary: NVIDIA's GeForce NOW got breached, exposing Armenian user data in what's becoming a depressingly familiar pattern. Even the graphics card gods aren't immune to basic security failures.

articles.title: Hackers ate my homework: Educational SaaS Canvas down after cyberattack
articles.summary: Meta mysteriously reversed course on Instagram encryption, making DMs plaintext again after years of promising end-to-end protection. Zuckerberg apparently decided privacy was bad for the surveillance capitalism business model.

articles.title: Big Finance Might Be Dooming the SPLC — Even Before Its Day in Court
articles.summary: The DOJ now treats FOIA evasion as a criminal offense worthy of arrest and strip searches—the ultimate irony from an administration that perfected transparency avoidance. Rules for thee, not for me reaches peak absurdity.

articles.title: AI Is Making Cyberattacks Cheaper, Faster and More Dangerous, IMF Warns
articles.summary: Quasar Linux RAT is hunting developers to poison the software supply chain with credential theft and keylogging. Because why compromise one system when you can backdoor everything they'll ever build?

articles.title: TCLBANKER Banking Trojan Targets Financial Platforms via WhatsApp and Outlook Worms
articles.summary: cPanel rushed fixes for three fresh vulnerabilities offering the holy trinity of privilege escalation, code execution, and DoS attacks. Web hosting just got a whole lot more exciting for all the wrong reasons.

articles.title: Congress Narrowed the GUARD Act, But Serious Problems Remain
articles.summary: Russian military hackers mass-harvested Microsoft Office tokens by exploiting ancient router vulnerabilities. When your network security is older than TikTok, you're basically serving credentials on a silver platter.

articles.title: Modeling individual self-protective behavior during epidemics
articles.summary: Mozilla used Anthropic's AI to identify and patch 423 Firefox security bugs in one month, proving that sometimes the robots are actually helpful. Still not a silver bullet, but hey—progress is progress.
